precepts.text: Have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.
precepts.point: Something you might not know: in the judge's chambers there are books on the wall, and those books have old cases. Your case might have the same case from 20 years ago. This is why the judge says, I'll be back with my decision. Some lawyers and prosecutors base their case on old cases. Where am I going with this? A judge is not always right. This is why they keep records, old records, so they can make the decision the right way. Some of you got a bishop in your camp, a captain in your camp, high ranking officers in your camp, and what did you do? You hide from them. These men are supposed to be your old records. And you know where you find the old records? The scriptures. Those are our records. When you ask Bishop a question, Bishop never gives you his opinion; he goes to the old records and makes them new to you. Where do you find the prophecies? In the old records.

note.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

precepts.why:
Moses charged the judges: “Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great”. You shall not have respect of persons in judgment; you cannot be partial. You have to hear both sides, the small as well as the great. That is the qualification of a judge, and if you are not ready for it, do not accept the position.

James speaks of the same thing: “My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.” Here is respect of persons, and James sets it against the faith of Christ itself. You cannot hold the faith of the Lord of glory and at the same time judge one brother by a different measure than another.

“ye shall not be afraid of the face of man”. You are not here to be loved or to be liked; you are judges. Some are afraid to make a decision because of what men will think of them, and some get offended when judgment falls on their friend, even without knowing what happened. What does that have to do with you? The judgment is God's, and a judge in Israel must be just, not partial.

precepts.text: The respect of persons goes into having a certain type of man in admiration over another, preferring one over another, and it shows in how you deal with matters with that brother. You are ready to have men's persons in admiration because of advantage: there's something you're going to gain by showing favoritism. And the end result: you are become judges of evil thoughts. Some brothers are horrible judges because there's something about the person they should judge that they can gain from them: they give you gifts, they're your ride to Sabbath, they got you a job. Now you are partial in your judgment because of what that person can provide for you. The Lord said that's an evil thing.

note.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

precepts.why:
“Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?” Respect of persons goes into having a certain type of man in admiration over another: respecting one over another, preferring one over another, and it shows in how you deal with matters with that brother or those brothers. You are ready to have men's persons in admiration for advantage; there is something you are going to gain by showing favoritism.

And here is the end result: you “are become judges of evil thoughts”. Some brothers are horrible judges because there is something about the person they should judge that they can gain from them. Whether he gives you gifts, whether he is your ride to Sabbath, whether he got you a job, whatever the case may be, now you are partial in your judgment because of what that person can provide for you. The Lord says that is an evil, evil thing.

So you might think, I am just not going to judge because that is my friend. The Bible says you are evil. That is exactly what Moses forbade when he charged the judges to “judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.”

precepts.text: We always hear thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not steal; we know those like the back of our hand. But it says if you have respect to persons, you commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors. You are breaking the commandments of God. You want the position, but there is much required from you in the position as judges. You must judge righteous judgment, whether it's your friend or not. You're in a position of leadership: you cannot conceal your friend's folly. What we've been discovering is that because someone is your friend, you don't want to reveal the sin, per Leviticus 5:1, and neither do you want to be a part of the judgment once the sin is revealed; you sit there quiet while the others bring out the transgressions, because you don't agree with the judgment that God says to bring forth. We have to stand on what God said. Anyone that you consider a friend goes against God and doesn't repent: I never knew you. Give us a little bit of time, we won't even remember your name, because you chose wickedness over the righteousness of God.

note.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

precepts.why:
“But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.” We always hear thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not steal; we know those like the back of our hand. But if you have respect of persons, whether in judgment or in having men's persons in admiration for advantage, you commit sin. You are a transgressor, breaking the commandments of God.

You want to be in that position, but much is required of you in the position as judges. You must judge matters and deal righteously, because that is the law of God we just read in Deuteronomy: judge righteous judgment, whether it is your friend or not. In a position of leadership you cannot conceal your friend's folly; none of us should.

What has been discovered is that because someone is your friend, you do not want to speak out. You do not want to reveal the sin, as Leviticus 5:1 requires, and you do not want to be part of the judgment once the sin is revealed. You sit there quiet while the others bring out the transgressions, because you do not agree with the judgment God says to bring forth. Something is wrong with that. We have to stand on what God said. Anyone you consider a friend who goes against God and does not repent: I never knew you. Give us a little time and we will not even remember his name, because he chose wickedness and evil over the righteousness of God.

precepts.text: God has chosen the poor of this world, robbed of nationality and land, to be rich in faith, because Christ came for us.
precepts.point: Every bomb dropped and every war fought loosens a link in the shackles of our captivity; the Lord is the director of this thing, and we should not be fearful when we see flames.

note.label: Eleutherophobia the Fear of Freedom

precepts.why:
Paul said we are “as poor, yet making many rich”. James shows why we are rich. They like to think this life we live is miserable. No: we are fulfilling God's prophecy.

“Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world”. How are we poor? Because they robbed us. We have been robbed of our nationality and robbed of our land. Israel is your land: black man, black woman, Latino man, Latino woman, Native American man, Native American woman. We did not know our nationality or our history. But that stops now; now we know.

“Rich in faith”. We are rich because Christ came for us; that is our faith. We keep the commandments and the faith of Jesus Christ, and we have the hope of deliverance coming our way: “heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him”.

That is why we are not fearful of freedom. Every bomb dropped and every war fought is loosening the links of the shackles of our captivity. The Lord is the director of this thing, and those he chose out of poverty are the heirs of the kingdom.

precepts.text: He that loveth another hath fulfilled the law: adultery, murder, theft, false witness, coveting and any other commandment are briefly comprehended in love thy neighbour as thyself; love worketh no ill to his neighbour and is the fulfilling of the law.
precepts.point: Whosoever shall keep the whole law and yet offend in one point is guilty of all: the Christian says you cannot keep them, but the context is the royal law, as the next verse shows, he that said do not commit adultery said also do not kill. Speak and do as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty, since Christ redeemed us from the death the moral law carried; he shall have judgment without mercy that hath showed no mercy.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
James 2:8 says “If ye fulfil the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well.” What is the royal law? Romans 13 lays it out.

“Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law.” What law? Love your neighbour as yourself. “For this, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness, Thou shalt not covet”: every one of those is the royal law. “And if there be any other commandment”, any other commandment regarding your neighbour outside of those, “it is briefly comprehended in this saying, namely, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.”

Love your neighbour as yourself is an abbreviation of the six commandments. Of the ten spoken commandments, the first four are how you observe God, and the last six are how you serve your neighbour: honour your father and mother, don’t commit adultery, don’t kill, don’t steal, don’t bear false witness, don’t covet. Those six are briefly comprehended in that one saying. The ten spoken commandments were themselves an abbreviation.

“Love worketh no ill to his neighbour”: no ill like being a respecter of persons, seating the man with the gold ring in a good place and telling the poor man to stand over there. “Therefore love is the fulfilling of the law.” Do we keep it? Yes, you simple Christians. That is the royal law James is talking about, and respect of persons is sin against it.

precepts.text: A lawyer, a scribe who copied the law and knew it, tempted Christ with the great commandment: love the Lord with all thy heart, the first four, and love thy neighbour as thyself, the six; on these two hang all the law and the prophets.
precepts.point: Whosoever shall keep the whole law and yet offend in one point is guilty of all: the Christian says you cannot keep them, but the context is the royal law, as the next verse shows, he that said do not commit adultery said also do not kill. note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“But when the Pharisees had heard that he had put the Sadducees to silence, they were gathered together.” Christ had put the Sadducees to shame, and the Pharisees saw how sharp he was. “Then one of them, which was a lawyer, asked him a question, tempting him.”

A lawyer is a scribe. Their job was writing the Bible over and over again, because ink fades and animal skin and paper rip and smear, so it had to be copied again and again. They were the recorders and copyists, and they knew the law and the prophets off top. That is why he was tempting Christ: he already knew the answer. “Master, which is the great commandment in the law?”

“Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment.” That is the first four of the ten spoken commandments. “And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.” That is the six, the royal law of James 2:8.

“On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.” These two are an abbreviation of all the laws. Loving God with all your heart, soul and mind means keeping the Sabbath day holy, the Passover, Tabernacles, Pentecost, the new moons, keeping the congregation, and the dietary law: don’t drink blood, don’t eat pork or shrimp. That is all serving God. The ten are an umbrella over all of them.

precepts.text: Mark adds the scribe's answer: to love God with all the heart and understanding and his neighbour as himself is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
Mark gives the same account with more detail, and it ties into sacrifice. “And one of the scribes came.” In Matthew he is called a lawyer; in Mark he is called a scribe, because they wrote things over and over and had the law in their minds. There were a bunch of them, but he was bold and spoke up: “Which is the first commandment of all?”

“The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord”: that is Deuteronomy 6:4. “And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment.” The commandments, the dietary law, the civil law, the sacrificial law, all of that is in there. “And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.” If you can keep those, you can keep them all.

“Well, Master, thou hast said the truth”: true, true, true. Then verse 33: “to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbour as himself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.” It is better than sacrifices. That is why Mark is loved: he makes it clear.

Why is it more than sacrifices? Because Israel would mess around, offer sacrifices, and then hate their neighbour, kill their neighbour, steal from their neighbour, bang their neighbour’s wife or sleep with their neighbour’s husband, but offer the best animal. The Lord said, I don’t care about that stuff. I care about your obedience, loving each other, loving me above the animals.

precepts.text: He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough, he that requiteth a good turn offereth fine flour, and to depart from wickedness is propitiation.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
Mark 12:33 said loving God and your neighbour is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices. Ecclesiasticus 35 says the same.

“He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.” Keeping the law is offering enough.

“He that requiteth a good turn offereth fine flour.” Under the offerings, you offered an animal, or fine flour if you were poor. Here, requiting a good turn, which is loving your neighbour as yourself, is the fine flour. “And he that giveth alms sacrificeth praise.”

“To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord; and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.” Propitiation means mercy, reconciliation. Departing from wickedness toward your neighbour is what reconciles you to God, which is why the royal law of James 2:8 stands above the sacrifices.

precepts.text: Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings as in obeying his voice? To obey is better than sacrifice, as Saul learned.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
Saul disobeyed a direct order, and through Samuel the Lord asks him a question: “Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord?” Answer it.

“Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.” The Lord cared about obedience more than animal sacrifices.

That is the same point as Mark 12:33, that loving God and your neighbour “is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.” Saul wanted to bring the sacrifice after he had disobeyed; Israel wanted to bring the best animal after they had wronged their neighbour. The Lord wants the obedience. And that is why James 2 holds us to the royal law, love thy neighbour as thyself, and not to an offering that covers over a sin against the brother.

precepts.text: Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: David learned the spirit that God does not care about sacrifice but obedience.

precepts.why:
“Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required.” This is quoted again in Hebrews 10.

David is saying, you opened my ears, and I understand the spirit: you don’t really care about sacrifices. Remember David wanted to build the temple. But the spirit was revealed to him that the sacrifices were just a placeholder for Christ to show up. He learned that because Christ was speaking through him.

So David realized: you don’t care about sacrifices at all, you care about obedience. That is what Samuel told Saul when he was king, “to obey is better than sacrifice.” And it is why the royal law of James 2, loving the neighbour and not being a respecter of persons, is what God is looking for.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice.”

To do justice and judgment, just like the Lord told Saul to do, is more acceptable than sacrifice. He says it over and over and over again: in Samuel, in the Psalms, in Mark, and here in Proverbs.

Justice and judgment is how you treat your neighbour. In James 2 the assembly seated the rich man in a good place and told the poor man to stand there, and James asks, “Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?” That is the opposite of doing justice and judgment, and no sacrifice would make up for it. Keeping the royal law is what is acceptable to the Lord.

precepts.text: I desired mercy and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings: the Lord said away with it through the prophets themselves.
precepts.point: Whosoever shall keep the whole law and yet offend in one point is guilty of all: the Christian says you cannot keep them, but the context is the royal law, as the next verse shows, he that said do not commit adultery said also do not kill. note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“Therefore have I hewed them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of my mouth.” The word of God can slay; it is the spirit. “And thy judgments are as the light that goeth forth.”

“For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.” He was not about the sacrifice. That was a schoolmaster, a placeholder. He desired mercy and the knowledge of God.

The Lord eventually said away with it, through the prophets themselves. And that is where James 2:13 lands: “For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.” You shall receive no mercy if you show no mercy. Mercy rejoices against judgment: the Most High chooses to have mercy rather than to judge you for violating the royal law, and he looks for that same mercy in us toward our neighbour.

precepts.text: All sacrifice is too little for a sweet savour, but he that feareth the Lord is great at all times.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“For all sacrifice is too little for a sweet savour unto thee, and all the fat is not sufficient for thy burnt offering: but he that feareth the Lord is great at all times.”

All sacrifice is too little. He that fears the Lord is great at all times. The Lord is saying, sacrificing, I don’t care about that; fearing me and obeying me is more important.

That closes the line of scriptures: Mark 12:33, Ecclesiasticus 35, 1 Samuel 15:22, Psalms 40:6, Proverbs 21:3, Hosea 6:6 and Judith 16:16 all say the same thing. Then back to James 2. “For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.” Christians use this to say that if you sin in one law you break them all, so you can’t keep them at all. But the context is the royal law, love your neighbour as yourself, and James explains it himself: “For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill.” If you commit no adultery but you kill your brother, you are a transgressor of the royal law.

“So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.” Under the old covenant, if you violated the moral law, moved your neighbour’s landmark or slept with your brother’s wife, you got death. Christ redeemed us from that and put us under the law of liberty. So stop doing it.

precepts.text: Everyone that shall be saved and escape by his works and by faith whereby ye have believed: works and faith, not one without the other.
precepts.point: Abraham was justified by works when he offered Isaac; faith wrought with his works and by works was faith made perfect, and he was called the friend of God. By works a man is justified and not by faith only, as Romans 2:13 said, and Rahab was justified by works when she sent the spies out another way. As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.” People say the law can’t save you, you are not justified by the works of the law. Ezra answers it: “And every one that shall be saved, and shall be able to escape by his works, and by faith, whereby ye have believed.”

Everyone that shall be saved shall escape by what? His works. And by faith. Works and faith go hand in hand; you have to have both, as James said. You will be saved by both: not faith alone and no works, not faith and no commandments, not commandments and no faith. That makes no sense; it is dead, being alone.

“though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?” That is like a man saying I got a paycheck, with no job. I get paid tomorrow. You got a job? No. It is the dumbest thing you can say out of your mouth. Your faith proves your works and your works prove your faith. Abraham had faith and kept the commandments of God, and his keeping the commandments proved his faith.

And it goes back to the royal law, loving your neighbour as yourself. Telling a brother with no food and no clothes “be ye warmed and filled”, and giving him nothing, makes no damn sense. Even so, faith without works makes no sense: the faith does not exist.

precepts.text: Here are they that keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus: the commandments are the works and Jesus is the faith.

By works a man is justified and not by faith only, as Romans 2:13 said, and Rahab was justified by works when she sent the spies out another way. As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works.” You cannot show faith without works. You show your faith through your actions, which is keeping the commandments of God. John says it in Revelation: “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.”

Keep the commandments, and the faith of Jesus. The faith is one, and the commandments are the works. That is what James said, and what Ezra said: saved by works and by faith.

“Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble.” Even the devils, the unclean spirits, believe in God and are afraid of him. “But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?” The vain man is the Christianity follower: faith without works, Calvinism, Protestantism, Catholicism. The saints are marked by both, the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus, and one without the other is dead.

precepts.why:
The saints “keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus”, and Revelation shows what the commandments are for: “Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.”

That do his commandments: deeds, actions, works. They must do the commandments to enter in through the gates, and have faith in Christ. They go hand in hand.

That is James’ point: “Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.” A man who says he has faith but does no works, who will not keep the commandments, has no right to the tree of life. Christ redeemed us from the death that came from breaking the law, and put us under the law of liberty, “So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.” The doing is what gives the right to enter the city.

precepts.text: Abraham believed God and it was counted unto him for righteousness.
precepts.point: Abraham was justified by works when he offered Isaac; faith wrought with his works and by works was faith made perfect, and he was called the friend of God. By works a man is justified and not by faith only, as Romans 2:13 said, and Rahab was justified by works when she sent the spies out another way. As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar?” Abraham was justified by his works because his works proved his faith. Offering Isaac was his action. “Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?” His faith was perfected by his works; he was proven faithful by them.

“And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness.” That is the scripture Paul quotes in Romans 4: “Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.” The same belief Paul speaks of is the belief James says was fulfilled when Abraham laid his son on the altar. His belief was counted for righteousness, and his works showed that belief to be real, “and he was called the Friend of God.”

So Paul and James do not disagree. “Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only”, which goes back to Romans 2:13, that the doers of the law shall be justified. Abraham believed, and kept the commandments of God, and both went together.

precepts.text: Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness.
precepts.point: Abraham was justified by works when he offered Isaac; faith wrought with his works and by works was faith made perfect, and he was called the friend of God. By works a man is justified and not by faith only, as Romans 2:13 said, and Rahab was justified by works when she sent the spies out another way. As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
James says “the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.” Paul quotes the same scripture to the Galatians: “Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness.”

Abraham’s belief was accounted for righteousness, and James shows how it was fulfilled: when he offered Isaac his son upon the altar. “Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?” Faith worked together with his actions, and his actions perfected it.

“Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only.” Rahab the harlot was justified the same way. She believed that if she helped the spies escape, they would spare her life; that was her faith, and receiving the messengers and sending them out another way was her works. “For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.” We have to keep the commandments and the faith of Christ; each goes with the other.

precepts.text: Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen. Substance is what you can touch. The student crossing campus with his T-squares and architect tubes has no degree yet, but the works of his mind tell you where he is going; that is how faith is validated by action. The Lord called the earth earth while it was without form and void because it existed in his mind, then the Spirit moved on the elements and formed it, and he compared the light to what he imagined and saw that it was good. Sisters do the same in the mirror, and walk away when the image matches the one in their mind. That is the power we have, and our elders were cut off from teaching us basics like that.
precepts.point: Our people in the world are raised to be slaves and statistics, fuel for the oppressor; when they see people who look like them building families, businesses, and healing on every level, they ask how, and you answer with the hope of your gospel: I was in a mess like you. When you come through these doors the brothers say welcome home, and I felt it: I never knew I was not home until I got there, and only then did the whole landscape make sense.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders & Fathers: the Children Are Listening

precepts.why:
“What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?” Can words save him? Because that is basically all you are giving. Some people don’t even understand what faith really is, because faith alone is just saying I believe in something. Paul defines it: “Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.”

So don’t tell me you have faith. Faith is the substance, and substance is what you can touch, what you can see, something materialized. You can have faith in your head all day long, underneath your skull; I can’t see it. The only way I will know what is in your mind is when I see action as a result of your thinking. As a man thinks, you are supposed to see the fruit of it.

Even if he or she has not achieved it yet, you can tell where they are going by how they carry themselves. On a college campus you see a student walking into the engineering building with his T-squares and architect tubes. He doesn’t have the degree yet, he is not an architect or engineer yet, but the works of his mind tell you where he is going. That is how faith is validated by action. Where there is no vision, the people perish; your mind has to manipulate the elements around you to form what you have in your head.

That is what the Lord did. The earth was without form and void, meaning it did not exist yet, but he still called it earth, because earth existed in God’s mind. Then the Spirit moved upon the face of the waters, the elements, and caused them to form the earth and the light. And he saw that the light was good: he compared what was formed to what he imagined and it agreed with the thought in his mind. Sisters do the same at the mirror; you don’t walk away until what you did with your hands matches the image in your mind, and then you say it is good. That is the power we have, but our elders were cut off from giving us basic understanding like that, and we fell asleep for centuries.

That is why the elders must set up organizational foundations, literal buildings where people can see the works of the teaching. A brother or sister naked and destitute of daily food told “Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled”, but given nothing, is still hungry. That is church, that is Christianity. “Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.”

precepts.text: Faith without works is dead; the works are the action of doing the commandments.
precepts.point: Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?” The works are the action of doing the commandments. Deuteronomy says “observe to do all his commandments and his statutes”, and do is the action word; the Most High is a God of doing.

Faith by itself, saying God knows my heart, is a dead faith. It is the doing of the commandments that gives faith its life, and it is the not doing that brings the curses.

precepts.text: As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.
precepts.point: Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.” A body with no spirit in it is a corpse, and faith with no works is the same. The works are the action of doing his commandments, which is exactly what Deuteronomy demands: “observe to do all his commandments and his statutes”.

The Most High is a God of doing, and by him actions are weighed. A faith that does not do the commandments is dead, and a people that does not do them falls under all these curses.

precepts.text: By works a man is justified, and not by faith only; Rahab the harlot was justified by works; faith without works is dead.
precepts.point: All the silver and gold and vessels of brass and iron were consecrated unto the Lord, separated and sanctified for his treasury alone: nobody was to gain personally from this war.

note.label: Joshua 6: The Fall of Jericho and the Faith of Rahab

precepts.why:
“only Rahab the harlot shall live, she and all that are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers that we sent.” She made a covenant with the spies: she would conceal them and assist Israel, knowing the Lord was with Israel, as long as her family was saved when the city fell. Rahab was a Canaanite, a heathen, yet the heathen can be blessed when they do it to benefit Israel; blessed is he that blesseth thee.

Rahab is the scripture's own example that a man is justified by works and not by faith only. “Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only. Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way? For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.”

Faith and works go hand in hand, for your actions prove whether you believe. Rahab did not only believe the Lord was with Israel; she received the messengers and sent them out another way, and that is why she lived.

precepts.text: Hath not God chosen the poor of this world, rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him? The Lord calls whom he will; money and status mean nothing to him.
precepts.point: The Lord commissions him: go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites; have not I sent thee? Gideon answers with his pedigree: my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house. That is a defeated mentality, and we all have to overcome it, because every one of us was called for a reason, to put a brick in for the kingdom.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
“Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him?”

Gideon's family was “poor in Manasseh”, and the Lord still said, “Go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites: have not I sent thee?” The Lord calls whom he will; money and status mean nothing to him. Rich, poor, or middle class, none of it matters to the Most High. The poor of this world are the ones he has chosen to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom.

precepts.text: He shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy, and mercy rejoiceth against judgment; Saul had just been shown mercy for his own failure, so passing merciless judgment on his own son would have left no mercy for Saul the next time he fell.
precepts.point: In some situations you have to weigh it like the people did: yes, he made a mistake and crossed the order, but he just saved all our lives.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

precepts.why:
The people stood up for Jonathan: “Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Israel? God forbid: as the Lord liveth, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground; for he hath wrought with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not.” They kept him from the wrath of his father.

Think about the contrast, and why the scripture says to get the love of the congregation. In chapter 13 Saul was the one disobeying the voice of the Lord and getting rebuked, while Jonathan was brave and mighty and had just saved Israel out of the hand of its enemies. Now the coward wants to kill the deliverer.

“For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.” Saul had just been shown mercy for his own failure, so passing merciless judgment on his own son would have left no mercy for Saul the next time he fell. In some situations you have to weigh it like the people did: yes, he made a mistake and crossed the order, but he just saved all our lives.

precepts.text: The devils also believe, and tremble; when Saul saw the spirit on David, he who sought David's life became the one afraid.
precepts.point: Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was with him and was departed from Saul. When Saul saw how quickly David escaped, that spirit on David made the hunter the scared one.

note.label: 1 Samuel 18: The Envious Eye of Saul

precepts.why:
James says, “the devils also believe, and tremble.” On the morrow “the evil spirit from God came upon Saul”, and this time it came back with more power: “there was a javelin in Saul’s hand. And Saul cast the javelin; for he said, I will smite David even to the wall with it. And David avoided out of his presence twice.”

When Saul saw how quickly David escaped, he saw the spirit on David, and he trembled: “Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was with him, and was departed from Saul.” The one seeking David's life became the one afraid. That spirit on David made the hunter the scared one.

precepts.text: He shall have judgment without mercy that hath shewed no mercy, and mercy rejoiceth against judgment; we rejoice when mercy is extended in the day we deserved punishment.
precepts.point: The afflicted people the Most High saves, but his eyes are upon the haughty to bring them down. The afflicted is Israel. He is David's lamp and lightens his darkness, for by the Most High David ran through a troop, a body of some two hundred men or more.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.”

David sang, “With the merciful thou wilt shew thyself merciful, and with the upright man thou wilt shew thyself upright. With the pure thou wilt shew thyself pure; and with the froward thou wilt shew thyself unsavoury.” What a man soweth, that shall he reap.

We all need mercy, so we must show mercy to one another, forgiving and not bearing grudges, that the Lord be merciful with us in the day of judgment. And we rejoice when mercy is extended in the day we deserved punishment.

precepts.text: The devils believe there is one God and tremble; the difference is the devils tremble at the fear of God, and in this flesh our people have a tendency not to fear Him.
precepts.point: A lot of times in Christianity people think everything bad comes from the devil and everything good comes from God. Wrong. Both good and evil come from the Lord. Satan is not a free spirit out here doing his own thing; he is subject to God, much like us.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

precepts.why:
“Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble.” The devils believe there is one God and tremble. That is what you see here: Satan is no free spirit out here doing his own thing. Job was the subject of discussion between Satan and the Lord, and Satan needed permission from the Lord to mess with him. “Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.” Satan is subject to God, much like us.

In Christianity they teach that Satan and God had a fight and Satan rebelled and took a third of the angels. That does not sound like what is right here. And a lot of times in Christianity people think everything bad comes from the devil and everything good comes from God. Wrong. Both good and evil come from the Lord.

The difference is the devils tremble at the fear of God, and in this flesh our people have a tendency not to fear him. Satan said Job only fears God because of the hedge about him and the blessing on the work of his hands: “put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.” That is the same thing with us today. When everything is going good you do not hear nothing from us; as soon as things go bad, that is when we start complaining and moaning and groaning.

precepts.text: Hold not the faith of Christ with respect of persons; favoring the rich man over the poor makes you a judge of evil thoughts.
precepts.point: We may not say the law is done away with, for if it were, righteous judgment would be done away with too, which makes no sense.

note.label: Proverbs 18: The Power of the Tongue and Righteous Judgment

precepts.why:
“My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.” Accepting the person of the wicked to overthrow the righteous in judgment is respect of persons, and the faith of Christ is not held that way.

Favoring the rich man over the poor makes you a judge of evil thoughts. The law of Leviticus 19 and the faith of Christ say the same thing.

precepts.text: If ye respect persons, ye commit sin and are convinced of the law as transgressors.
precepts.point: We may not say the law is done away with, for if it were, righteous judgment would be done away with too, which makes no sense.

note.label: Proverbs 18: The Power of the Tongue and Righteous Judgment

precepts.why:
“But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.” Respect of persons is sin, and it is the law that convinces the one who does it as a transgressor.

So the law is not done away with; James judges respect of persons by it. To accept the person of the wicked and overthrow the righteous in judgment is to be convinced of the law as a transgressor.

points: But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors. A lot of times brothers do not speak up because, Bishop always says, that friendship with a T. You let that govern you. You let that take over. You are not dealing right.

If you have respect of persons, because this is my boy, so I am going to slide him this little money on the side, because I know he is going through hard times, out of the offerings, the congregation's money. The little benevolence pay on the side. The scripture says the Lord identifies you as a transgressor. That is having respect of persons.
They become cliquish. Certain people get special privileges, meaning sin-wise they get away with it. You watch them judge other people harshly, but over here this one gets a pass. No, bro.

You have favouritism. A principle in leadership: favouritism destroys trust, because it teaches the people that relationships and rank matter more than being righteous. It matters more than doing what God said to do. All these principles are small principles that encompass how you are going to be viewed as a leader, how people are going to respect what you say, how they are going to buy into the system and say, you know what, you are worth following, because you are following what the scripture says. There is nothing that I am saying that we ourselves do not apply. And if we are not applying it, may God deal with us. It is not a game. It is not, he likes me, or I like him. The Bible says that, and what side do you stand on? I am reading this and you are doing that. You are in error with God, and that is just what it is. Now there is a way to fix it: get back in line with these scriptures.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

If a brother or sister be naked and destitute of daily food, and one of you say unto them, depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled, notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body, what doth it profit? Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.

note.label: Member's In The Body

points: Hearken, my beloved brethren, hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him? Why are we rich in faith? Because God chose you. He called you; he requested you.

In the time of our oppression, faith is the only thing that is going to keep us together, and you are not alone: your brother, your sister, your nation. Coming to keep the Sabbath builds your faith. Seeing us go to various places on the planet and fulfill the prophecies of God, seeing our people understand this word abroad, that builds your faith: not trust in man, but trust that God's prophecies are being fulfilled.
Them that love him keep his commandments and show it with their faith, preparing our minds for the return of our Messiah.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

points: The fifth mark: a leader leads by example. Faith without works is dead; I will show thee my faith by my works.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

points: Have not the faith of Christ with respect of persons: seating the man in the gold ring and the fine clothing and telling the poor man to stand there is being partial and a judge of evil thoughts, and it violates loving thy neighbour. God has chosen the poor of this world, us, rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom, while the rich Pharisee and the white man oppress you and blaspheme Christ's name.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

points: If ye fulfil the royal law, thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well; respect of persons is sin against it. Love thy neighbour is the abbreviation of the six commandments toward man, as the first four are toward God, and on love God and love thy neighbour hang all the law and the prophets: Sabbath, feasts, new moons and dietary law are loving God. Loving God and neighbour is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices, because Israel would offer the best animal and then kill their neighbour and sleep with his wife.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

points: Whosoever shall keep the whole law and yet offend in one point is guilty of all: the Christian says you cannot keep them, but the context is the royal law, as the next verse shows, he that said do not commit adultery said also do not kill. Speak and do as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty, since Christ redeemed us from the death the moral law carried; he shall have judgment without mercy that hath showed no mercy.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

points: Though a man say he hath faith and have not works, can faith save him? Like a man with a paycheque and no job. Telling a naked and hungry brother be warmed and filled without giving him what he needs profits nothing, and even so faith without works is dead, being alone. Abraham's faith and his keeping the commandments went together.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

points: Show me thy faith without thy works and I will show thee my faith by my works: faith is shown by keeping the commandments. The devils also believe and tremble; the vain man of faith without works is Calvinism, Protestantism and Catholicism.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

points: Abraham was justified by works when he offered Isaac; faith wrought with his works and by works was faith made perfect, and he was called the friend of God. By works a man is justified and not by faith only, as Romans 2:13 said, and Rahab was justified by works when she sent the spies out another way. As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

points: The elders' serious job is setting up organizational foundations: literal buildings and institutions where people can see the works of your teaching. Tell someone in the street to repent and they ask where the sanctuary is; you cannot send them to the internet. Bishop Nathanyel said in 2015, over the New York building, that any leader not thinking forwardly about building and directing institutions is a waste of time. As a man thinks, you should see action from it; anyone, women, men, friends, or family, who threatens that, you separate from.

What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? Can faith save him? Faith in your head that I cannot see might as well not be there; I only know what is in your mind when I see action. As a man thinketh, he becomes what he thinks.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders & Fathers: the Children Are Listening

points: If a brother or sister be naked and destitute of daily food, and one of you say, depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled, notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body, what doth it profit? Be warmed and filled with my great words: the man is still hungry. That is church; that is Christianity. Notwithstanding means not validated, no value. Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone: faith does not exist without works attached, and anyone preaching faith without works is lying.
